section.title: Everything you want to know
section.support_prefix: Don't see your question? Reach out via

left.q: What if someone removes the Frame-ID from my bike?
left.a:
First of all, that's not easy: the Frame-ID is designed to break apart on removal attempts — the material crumbles into pieces and also damages the frame's paint. Every attempt leaves clear traces.

But even if someone succeeds: at registration we also store the brand and frame number of your bike. Your bike stays traceable through that combination — just like a car without a licence plate can still be found via its chassis number. The Frame-ID just makes it faster and easier.

On top of that, Velopass blocks any attempt to re-register a bike that's already known, based on the brand + frame number combination. A thief therefore cannot re-register your bike under their name.

Want to check if your bike is registered? Search by brand + frame number on [Bike check →](/bike-check)

left.q: Can I order a new Frame-ID if mine was removed or damaged?
left.a: Yes. Order a new Frame-ID through our webshop or at a Velopass bike shop near you. Once it arrives, log in to your Velopass, select the bike and click 'Replace Frame-ID'. Your bike history and all active services stay intact.

left.q: How do I transfer my bike to a new owner?
left.a: Log in to your Velopass, select the bike and click 'Transfer ownership'. You'll receive a PIN by email. Share that PIN with the new owner — they enter it and the bike is registered in their name. The full bike history transfers with it — only your personal details and private photos stay private.

left.q: How does Velopass work with the Belgian National Bike Register (MyBike)?
left.a: You can use your Velopass code to also register your bike in MyBike, the Belgian national bike register. That way you're doubly protected — both in the Velopass Community and in the official register.

left.q: What's the difference between the Velopass code and the frame number?
left.a: They are two different numbers. The frame number is the serial number the manufacturer has engraved on your bike's frame. The Velopass code is on the Frame-ID stuck to your bike and gives access to your digital passport. On bikesearch.velopass.com you can search using either.

right.q: What do ALL CLEAR, REPORTED and NOT REGISTERED mean?
right.a:
These are the three statuses in the Velopass Community:
• ALL CLEAR: the bike is registered and not reported missing. All good.
• REPORTED: the owner has actively reported the bike. The community is helping look.
• NOT REGISTERED: the bike is not in the Velopass database and is not yet protected.

right.q: Why is engraving no longer used and what's the difference with Velopass?
right.a:
Engraving has nearly disappeared — and rightly so. Modern carbon or aluminium bikes get damaged by an engraving machine. On carbon, engraving is even fatal to the frame structure. E-bikes also have internal cables running through the tubes.

In the past, your national ID number was engraved — that's a privacy risk. Your personal ID was literally visible on your bike.

The Velopass Frame-ID replaces this entirely:
• No damage to the frame — the sticker adheres, it doesn't scratch
• No personal data on the sticker — anyone scanning sees only the status (free or reported), never your data
• Tamper-resistant — the material crumbles to pieces if someone tries to remove it
• Transferable — at resale you hand over the digital passport to the new owner, without re-registering
• Digital passport — proof of purchase, serial number and maintenance history all in one place

right.q: I'm trying to log in but it doesn't work.
right.a: The app in the App Store and Google Play is the Velopass Pro app — exclusively for bike shops. As a cyclist you log in via velopass.com. Click 'Log in' top right or go to app.velopass.com/login.

right.q: I'm buying a second-hand bike with a Velopass Frame-ID. What should I do?
right.a: Two steps. Before the purchase: check the bike's status on bikesearch.velopass.com — that way you're sure the bike isn't reported stolen or missing. After the purchase: ask the previous owner to transfer ownership to you via their Velopass account. Then the bike is officially in your name.

right.q: How do I link a bike shop to my Velopass?
right.a: If your bike was registered through a Velopass bike shop, that shop is already linked automatically. Want to pick another shop or add a shop? Do it in your Velopass account under 'My bike shop'. You can change this at any time.

There are two situations where registration works differently:

Does your Velopass code start with VP? Then you most likely bought it in France. In France, bike registration is required by law and must be done by the seller — the bike shop. The shop registers the bike at sale; you can't do this yourself online. Contact your bike shop if registration hasn't happened yet.

Is it a lease bike? Lease bikes are registered in the leasing company's name (Joule is an exception — there you do have your own account). In that case you don't have your own Velopass account, but the bike shop can read your bike and add maintenance. Is your bike lost or stolen? Report it to the leasing company — they can mark the bike as missing.
